description: Station proofs of the example network of section 6, its operator holding the quorum of section 6, signed with the Ed25519 keys of section 6 and two seeds of their own: what a verifier must take and refuse, checked against a trust anchor at a point in time. Trust anchors and proofs are JSON text, to be read as POI reads JSON.

stationProofs.description: Attested by the signing keys of both holders, each certified by the identity key of its holder, which the trust anchor pins; within the validity of the attestations.
A minute after the attestations ended (validUntil).
A second before the attestations were signed, the key statement and the certificates valid: an attestation of the future is no attestation now.
Attested by Alpha only, where the quorum takes two holders.
Attested twice by the signing key of Alpha: one holder.
Alpha attests the root, Beta only the digest of DE*GEF (a subject): a subject attests one entity, not the root, and does not count for the proof.
Beta attests the root in the role of a witness: the roaming network operator attests its versions.
Attestations without validUntil, two weeks later, the key statement and the certificates still valid: an attestation gives its validUntil, so that none is valid forever.
Attestations valid for 24 hours, the longest an attestation is valid, an hour before they end.
Attestations valid for 24 hours and a millisecond, checked within them: an attestation is valid for 24 hours at most.
The certificate of the signing key of Beta names another roaming network operator.
The key statement names another roaming network operator.
The signing key of Beta may sign tariffs only, not for the party.
The signing key of Beta expired before it attested (notAfter).

The signing key of Beta ended (notAfter) after it attested and before the time checked, its attestation still valid: the key of an attestation is valid when it attested and when it is checked, its signedAt being the choice of its signer.
The signing key of Beta certified by the identity key of Alpha: each holder certifies its own signing keys only.
Beta attests with a key no certificate names.
A trust anchor pinning other identity keys.
A trust anchor of minConsensus 1, Alpha alone attesting: the quorum of the key statement, two, is the larger.
Beta attests a version of another roaming network.
The EVSE changed after the attestations: the proof leads to another root than they attest.
The signature of Beta replaced by the one of Alpha.
The trust anchor names the two identity keys of Alpha as one holder, the key statement names both as keys of Alpha and is signed by the second one and by Beta; attested by Alpha and Beta.

Alpha names its second identity key as one of Beta in a key statement it signs with both, certifies a signing key of "Beta" with that key and attests with both signing keys: the trust anchor names both identity keys as one holder, the statement names their holders otherwise and is refused.

The key statement, signed by Alpha and Beta, names the second identity key of Alpha only; the operator names the first one as one of "Beta", which certifies a signing key of "Beta": the trust anchor names that key as one of Alpha, so its attestation counts for Alpha, and Alpha alone attests.
